name: pager
description: UIDS pager component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3). One 'Pager Item' component with a 2-value State axis (Default, Active) — smaller than the survey's 3x5 = 15 estimate (State x Context). The four ancestor-context looks are documentation frames on the component's page, not set variants. See openQuestions for the richer 2x5 = 10 alternative.
axisRationale: The survey's claimed 'Button/Brand-Bar precedent' for collapsing ancestor-background context into an axis DOES NOT EXIST — verified by reading both contracts in full. button.json's axes are Color/Size/Style, all describing the button's own props, with ancestor-background reactivity in prose only. brand-bar.json's Style/Healthcare/Breakpoint describe the bar's own inherent state, not reaction to an ambient wrapper. See claims (precedent-check).
Disabled has no confirmed producer in either live Drupal template (see claims: unreachable), matching the established precedent of not modelling unreachable classes as variant values.

Context looks are composed instances rather than set variants — the same treatment Headline gives its un-propped negative/center looks. See openQuestions for the richer State x Context = 10 alternative, which would be a NEW pattern rather than a continuation of an existing one.

options.name: state
options.description: Per-item visual state. Pager.vue derives is-active from the current page number; production Twig derives the same class from Drupal pager state.

code.notes: No direct state prop exists. The current Number prop selects which generated item receives is-active. Disabled remains excluded because neither Vue nor production Twig produces it.

figma.notes: Disabled is not a State value — shown, if at all, as a documentation frame on the component's Figma page, not a variant (see figmaProposal).

options.name: current
options.description: Current page; drives the is-active item plus first/previous/next/last visibility.

figma.notes: Selects the Active item in the composed pager; not a component-set axis.

options.name: total
options.description: Total page count used to clamp the visible window.

options.name: quantity
options.description: Maximum number of page-number links shown at once.

options.name: heading_id
options.description: ID joining the navigation landmark to its visually-hidden heading.

slots.name: item
slots.description: One pager entry's visible content: a page number, a first/previous/next/last icon+label pair (BEM pager__item--first/--previous/--next/--last), or the ellipsis glyph.
slots.behavior:
All item types share IDENTICAL DOM/CSS structure (
  • ...
    • ) and differ only in label text/icon glyph — pager.scss has no per-item-type selector. Modelled as a text/icon property, not a Figma axis, matching how Button's label is a text layer. The mini-pager's current-page item is the ONE exception: views-mini-pager.html.twig renders it as plain text with NO nested at all, so `.pager .is-active a` never matches there — only the full pager's current-page
  • contains a real anchor.

figma.notes: One 'Pager Item' component instanced repeatedly (with State variants) to compose a documentation row, the same compositional pattern Brand-Footer uses for repeated Logo instances, rather than one fixed giant component.

behavior: Pager.vue mirrors uids_base pager.html.twig and derives a centered, clamped page window from current/total/quantity. It renders first/previous/next/last only when those destinations exist and uses BEM ellipsis items with literal glyphs.
Context colors are driven by ancestor bg--black/gold/gray/white classes, not a Pager prop. The OnBackgrounds story documents those contexts without adding a Figma axis.
The full current-page item contains an anchor and receives is-active; aria-current=page is applied to that anchor. Production mini-pager markup differs by rendering its current page as plain text.
The local Vue component imports pager.scss for Storybook/package use, but SiteNow production still compiles its independently maintained pagination.scss fork with a 40em display gate.
knownIssues: margin-bottom: $sm (pager.scss:5, inside the first .pager{} rule) never renders — permanently overridden by the later, equal-specificity .pager{margin-bottom:$mobile-height-gutter} at pager.scss:78 (confirmed: dart-sass compile of the file shows margin-bottom exactly once in output, valued 2rem). margin-left:0 from that SAME rule is untouched and DOES render — see claims (specificity-dead).

Several declarations are restated, at equal specificity, between the original block and the later 'uids_base styles' block with no rendering difference: .pager a's color (pager.scss:41 & :83), the .pager a:hover/.pager button:hover background (pager.scss:47, superseded for 'a' only, at :99), and .is-active a's base color/background plus hover values (pager.scss:52-56 vs :112-113/:127-128). One override, [class*=bg--gray]/[class*=bg--white] forcing is-active's color to $white (pager.scss:115-118), is an outright no-op: is-active already sets color:$white unconditionally two lines earlier in the SAME block (pager.scss:113) — see claims (redundant, four entries).

`.pager .disabled`/`.pager .disabled:hover` (pager.scss:60-68) and `.pager .ellipsis::after` (pager.scss:70-74) target classes that neither Drupal core's nor uids_base's actual pager.html.twig/views-mini-pager.html.twig ever emit — unavailable pages are omitted from the markup entirely (never rendered disabled), and the real ellipsis is a BEM `pager__item--ellipsis` <li> with the glyph as literal text, not this class+::after pattern. Tokenized as-shipped anyway (pager/disabled/color, pager/ellipsis/color) — this is a markup-reachability gap, not CSS-cascade specificity-dead code, so this batch's tokenization rule does not exempt it (see the pager/disabled/color entry for the precedent this reasoning rests on). See claims (unreachable).

On a bg--black ancestor, pager's own file supplies only background-color:$secondary (black) for the plain link (pager.scss:84-86), leaving the inherited color:$secondary (black) from pager.scss:41/:83 in place — black-on-black, if pager's file were the only stylesheet in play. Readable rendering depends entirely on a SEPARATE stylesheet: the Background foundation's `.bg--black a { color: ... }` rule (compiled from _background-mixins.scss's bg-fg-colors mixin, 'dark' branch, _background-mixins.scss:111-115), generated as `--uiowa-color-on-dark-link: var(--brand-primary)` (_tokens-generated.scss:105, backing the ALREADY-SHIPPED tokens/semantic/colors.json color.on-dark.link token) — i.e. GOLD, fully readable. That rule sits at the SAME specificity tier as pager's own (.bg--black a vs .pager a: one class-or-attribute-selector + one element each), so the winner is whichever stylesheet loads LATER. In uids_base's actual production build this is resolved by Drupal library weight, not by anything pager's own file guarantees: assets/css/components/background.css is attached with an explicit weight:200 (uids_base.libraries.yml:34) while assets/css/components/pagination.css has the default weight 0 (uids_base.libraries.yml:21), so background.css loads later and its rescue rule wins. Confirmed consistent in BOTH the current 4.x branch (token-generated, resolves to gold) and production's currently-compiled snapshot (older, pre-token version, hardcodes the same var(--brand-primary) directly) — so the rescue is real and currently intact, but load-order-dependent rather than something pager's own rule guarantees by itself. No equivalent risk exists for the other three contexts: white/gray/gold ancestors' 'light' on-light.link role also resolves to black ({color.black}, tokens/semantic/colors.json), the SAME color pager already sets itself, so there is nothing to rescue there.

Colors.stories.js (Foundation/Colors, tags:['!autodocs']) documents an aspirational, UNIMPLEMENTED 'Gray Palette v2' renumbering with two internal inconsistencies bearing directly on pager: (1) its deprecatedRows table's entry that literally says 'Migrate PAGER disabled states to $gray-50 background and $gray-500 text' is attached to the `$light-gray` row (#B3B3B3, color.scale($blk,70%)) — a variable pager.scss does NOT use anywhere (grep-confirmed: zero uses outside its own _variables.scss:33 definition and this one stories.js reference) — while the variable pager ACTUALLY uses, `$gray-light` (#CACACA), has its own separate, more generic note not naming pager specifically; (2) the story's proposed 'gray-50'/'gray-500' labels collide with DIFFERENT, already-shipped tokens/primitives/colors.json keys of the identical name (color.gray.50 = #FAFAFB, forms input background; color.gray.500 = #63666A, cool gray) — naively adopting the aspirational scheme's names would silently swap in the wrong hex under a familiar-looking key. This spec tokenizes pager's disabled state under its CURRENT primitive (gray.200) rather than the aspirational scheme — see claims (documentation-bug, two entries) and openQuestions.

pager.scss's utilities.padding()/margin() mixin calls prefix every keyword-argument name with the `variables.` module namespace (e.g. utilities.padding(variables.$top: variables.$sm, ...), pager.scss:5,25,42,63,73) — unique to this file; every other component uses the plain $top: ... form. Verified harmless: _utilities.scss's mixins (:95,:102) declare plain unnamespaced parameters, `variables.$top` does not exist as a real variable (compiling it standalone throws dart-sass's Undefined-variable error), yet the full file compiles to byte-correct padding/margin output — dart-sass silently accepts and discards a namespace prefix immediately before a keyword-argument name. Purely stylistic; worth normalizing during migration.
The draft spec predated Pager.vue and described Pager as a local build orphan. That is no longer true after aa71cff490; only the downstream production pagination.scss divergence remains.

geometryNotTokenized.clearfix-pseudo-elements: `.pager::before, .pager::after { display:table; order:1; content:' '; flex:1 0 0; }` and `.pager::after { clear:both; }` (pager.scss:11-21) — float/flex containment mechanics, not a design value.
geometryNotTokenized.outer-margin: margin-left:0 (pager.scss:5, survives — see knownIssues), margin-bottom:2rem (pager.scss:78, = $mobile-height-gutter = the EXISTING, non-deferred space.200 primitive) and margin-top:1.5rem (pager.scss:79, raw literal with no named Sass var, coincidentally = space.150). Left as raw geometry matching Button/Headline's precedent of not tokenizing a component's own outer placement margin; both primitive-equivalents are noted here for a future pass, not promoted to tier-3 in this spec (see openQuestions if this default should flip for the gutter value specifically, since it is a genuinely shared, already-tokenized primitive rather than a one-off magic number).
geometryNotTokenized.list-item-and-link-padding: li margin-right ($xsm) and the a/button/.disabled/.ellipsis padding-block ($sm) / padding-inline ($md) — see sharedPrimitiveUsage. Deliberately NOT re-minted as tier-3, per tokens/README's explicit $xsm...$xxxlg-are-primitives rule (matches Headline's identical treatment of its own $sm use in underline-padding-bottom).
geometryNotTokenized.state-cursors-and-keywords: cursor:not-allowed (.disabled, pager.scss:61), cursor:default (.is-active a, pager.scss:51), background:transparent (.disabled:hover, pager.scss:67) — CSS keyword values, not color/dimension tokens.
geometryNotTokenized.ellipsis-glyph: content:'\2026' (pager.scss:71) — a literal Unicode ellipsis character, not a design token; moot regardless since the rule is unreachable (see claims).
